info.title: BE Auction API
info.description: API documentation for the BE Auction platform.

amount.description: Amount to withdraw in VND decimal string (pays out 100%, no fee)

overdue.description: Filter for pending/processing requests exceeding 10-day deadline (true/false)

proof_file_id.description: File ID of the bank transfer receipt uploaded via file module

status.description: Omit to list every publicly visible auction. `cancelled` is filtered out server-side and returns nothing even when asked for explicitly.

isDefault.description: Promotes this address to the user's default, demoting the previous one. The first address a user creates becomes the default regardless.

UpdateAddressDto.description: Every field is optional; only the ones supplied are written.

isDefault.description: Only `true` is meaningful — a user always keeps exactly one default.

status.description: Target status. Any other value is rejected: `open` is what GET /support-chat/my-chat looks for and what the one-open-ticket-per-user constraint is keyed on, so an unrecognised status hides the ticket from the user and lets them open a second one.

orderId.description: ID of the delivered order being reviewed. One review per order.

shippingRating.description: Optional rating of the shipping experience

serviceRating.description: Optional rating of the seller's service

isAnonymous.description: Hide the reviewer's identity from public listings

mediaFileIds.description: Ids returned by POST /api/v1/files (purpose: review). The review response carries presigned URLs for them; no URL is ever stored.

comment.description: The reviewed seller's public reply. One reply per review.
comment.example: Thanks for your feedback — glad the item arrived safely!

reason.description: Recorded in the admin audit log, not shown to the author.

categoryId.description: New category ID for the product

status.description: Filter by product status (usually for /me/products endpoint)

search.description: Search term to filter by product name

images.description: List of images with their new display orders. Must contain all images for the product.

deviceId.description: Unique device identifier for multi-device session management. Generated by server if not provided.

userName.description: Letters, numbers, dot, underscore and hyphen only. An email address is not accepted: usernames are shown publicly, for example on an auction's bidder list, while the email stays private.

refreshToken.description: Long-lived JWT refresh token (default 7d). Contains deviceId in payload.

avatarFileId.description: Id in `files`. Use GET /api/v1/files/{id}/url to re-sign avatarUrl once it expires.

avatarUrl.description: Presigned URL, valid for 1 hour. Do not persist it.

actionType.description: Filters on the bid row itself. Not the same axis as `auctionStatus`: "still running" is a property of the auction, not of the bid.

auctionStatus.description: Pass `happening` for the bids that are still in play.

sortBy.description: `position` is not sortable — it is the rank recorded when the row was written and is nullable, so ordering by it is not stable.

search.description: Matches the product name, case-insensitively. Wildcards are escaped.

dateFrom.description: ISO 8601 date-time, or a bare `YYYY-MM-DD`. Filters on the BID's createdAt, not the auction's. Inclusive.

dateTo.description: Same formats as `dateFrom`, and inclusive. A bare date covers the whole day — `2026-09-20` includes bids placed at 23:59 that day, rather than cutting off at midnight.

limitBid.description: Ceiling the proxy may bid up to on your behalf. The server picks every actual bid amount; the step comes from the auction's own bidIncrement. Kept private to you — other bidders never see it.

limit.description: Number of suggestions to return. This endpoint feeds the header search dropdown, so it is deliberately capped and has no paging.

status.description: Filter by auction status. Omit to search only auctions a user can still act on — live and upcoming ones.

quantity.description: Units sold as one lot to a single winner, so every price below is for the whole lot, not per unit.

UpdateAuctionRequestDto.description: Every field optional; only what you send is changed. The product cannot be swapped — withdraw the request and file a new one instead.

reason.description: Shown to the seller, so it has to say something useful.

search.description: Admin listing only — matches the product name.

status.description: Filter by auction status. Omit to list every status.

sortBy.description: Sort field. Omit to keep the status-aware default: ended auctions newest-first, live and upcoming ones closing-soonest-first.

sortOrder.description: Sort order. Defaults to desc when sortBy is given.

search.description: Matches the product name, case-insensitively. Wildcards are escaped.

year.description: Calendar year to report on. Defaults to the current year.

Wallet.description: The user's wallet. Every registered user has exactly one wallet.

balance.description:
Current available balance in VND, decimal(14,2) as string.
This is a cached value; the source of truth is `SUM(wallet_ledger.amount)`.
Pending withdrawal holds have already been subtracted.

status.description:
`active` — normal operations allowed.
`locked` — wallet frozen (fraud/dispute). All debit and credit operations will be rejected with 403.

LedgerEntry.description:
A single append-only ledger entry recording a balance movement.
Positive amount = credit (money in), negative = debit (money out), zero = book-closing marker.

type.description:
Ledger entry type. Determines the nature of the movement:
- `topup_success` — Bank transfer confirmed via Sepay webhook (+)
- `payment` — Buyer pays for an order (−)
- `payment_escrow_in` — Money enters platform escrow (+)
- `payment_release` — Seller receives payout after 5% fee (+)
- `payment_escrow_out` — Money leaves platform escrow (−)
- `platform_fee` — 5% commission retained by platform (+)
- `payment_refund` — Buyer refunded before release (+)
- `withdraw_hold` — Balance held when withdrawal requested (−)
- `withdraw_success` — Withdrawal completed, book closed (0)
- `withdraw_failed` — Withdrawal rejected, hold refunded (+)
- `withdraw_cancelled` — User cancelled withdrawal, hold refunded (+)
- `adjustment` — Manual admin reconciliation (±)

amount.description:
Signed decimal amount. Positive = credit, negative = debit, zero = marker.
Always a string with 2 decimal places.

balanceAfter.description: Wallet balance snapshot immediately after this entry was posted

referenceId.description: ID of the referenced entity (polymorphic FK)

idempotencyKey.description:
Unique key ensuring this entry is written at most once.
Format: `{type}:{reference_id}` (e.g. `sepay:TX123`, `order_payment:42`).

metadata.description: Extra context — admin_id, reject_reason, fee_rate, bank_reference, etc.

nextCursor.description:
Opaque base64-encoded cursor for the next page. Pass this as `?cursor=` to fetch more.
`null` when there are no more results.

TopupResponse.description: Instructions for the user to complete a bank transfer top-up

transactionId.description: ID of the pending Transaction row created for tracking

paymentCode.description:
Transfer note the user MUST include in their bank transfer.
Format: `BIDYTOPUP{transactionId padded to 3 digits}` (e.g. `BIDYTOPUP088`).
The Sepay webhook matches this code to credit the correct wallet.

qrCodeUrl.description: VietQR image URL — display this as a scannable QR code

bankInfo.description: Bank account details for manual transfer

UserSummary.description: Aggregated financial summary grouped by ledger entry type

byType.description:
Map of ledger type → { totalAmount, count }.
Only types that have at least one entry are included.

totalAmount.description: Sum of all amounts for this type (signed)

count.description: Number of entries of this type

WithdrawalRequest.description: A request to withdraw funds from the wallet to a bank account

amount.description:
Amount to withdraw. This is the **exact** amount that will be bank-transferred.
No fees are deducted at withdrawal — the 5% platform fee was already collected at escrow release.

bankAccountName.description: Account holder name (as registered with the bank)

status.description:
Lifecycle:
- `pending` — Created, balance already held. User may cancel.
- `processing` — Admin acknowledged, preparing bank transfer. User can no longer cancel.
- `completed` — Admin confirmed bank transfer done (proof_file_id attached).
- `rejected` — Admin rejected. Full amount refunded to wallet.
- `cancelled` — User cancelled. Full amount refunded to wallet.

cancelledBy.description: Who initiated the cancellation. Null if not cancelled.

deadlineAt.description:
SLA deadline = created_at + 10 days. Admin should process before this date.
Exceeding this triggers hourly cron alerts but does NOT auto-cancel.

proofFileId.description: File ID of the bank transfer receipt (uploaded via file module). Present only when completed.

proofUrl.description: Fresh presigned URL of the bank transfer receipt. Minted on read via FileService. Present only when completed.

rejectReason.description: Reason provided by admin when rejecting

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. `null` = no more results.

sourceBreakdown.description: Display-only breakdown of where the user's money came from

salesRevenue.description: Sum of all released sales proceeds net of fees (payment_release)

totalUserLiability.description: Benchmark SUM(wallets.balance) across ALL wallets to compare against real bank account before transferring

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. `null` = no more results.

AdminOverview.description:
Aggregated financial overview from `wallet_daily_summary` table.
This endpoint reads pre-computed daily summaries (generated nightly at 01:00),
NOT the full ledger — so it is fast even with millions of entries.

totalTopup.description: Sum of all top-ups in the date range

totalPayment.description: Sum of all payments (absolute value) in the date range

totalWithdraw.description: Sum of all withdrawal holds (absolute value) in the date range

totalPlatformFee.description: Sum of all 5% platform fees collected in the date range

activeWallets.description: Number of wallets with activity on the most recent day in the range

dailySummaries.description: Individual daily breakdowns, sorted by date descending

DailySummary.description: Pre-aggregated daily financial summary (generated by nightly cron at 01:00 UTC)

activeWallets.description: Count of distinct wallets with ledger activity on this date

EscrowReport.description:
Escrow audit report showing all orders with funds held in escrow.
Orders are sorted by `delivered_at ASC NULLS LAST` so the **oldest delivered but unreleased**
orders appear first — these are the ones most likely needing admin attention.

Includes Invariant 3 verification: platform wallet balance must be ≥ total held escrow.

totalEscrow.description: Total amount currently held in escrow across all orders

platformWalletBalance.description:
Current balance of the platform wallet. Must be ≥ `totalEscrow`.
If lower, there is a financial integrity issue.

isEscrowCovered.description:
`true` if `platformWalletBalance >= totalEscrow` (Invariant 3 holds).
**If `false`, this is a CRITICAL alert** — the platform cannot cover all pending payouts.

orders.description:
Paginated list of held orders. Sorted by:
1. `delivered_at ASC NULLS LAST` — delivered orders that haven't been released surface first
2. `created_at ASC` — oldest first within each group

items.description: Order with escrow held (subset of Order fields relevant to escrow)

delivered_at.description: When the order was marked as delivered. `null` = not yet delivered.

nextCursor.description: Cursor for next page of orders

AdjustmentResult.description:
Result of a manual balance adjustment. This is a ledger entry with type `adjustment`.
Used for reconciliation when the Sepay webhook was missed, or to correct mistakes.

amount.description: Signed amount. Positive = credit, negative = debit.

reason.example: Bank transfer confirmed on statement but webhook failed

StoredProductImage.description: One product image. The bucket is private, so `imageUrl` is minted per response and expires; `fileId` is the durable handle.

id.description: product_images row id, used by the reorder/primary endpoints.

fileId.description: Id in the files table. Use GET /api/v1/files/:id/url to re-sign `imageUrl` once it expires, without refetching the product.

imageUrl.description: Presigned URL, valid for 1 hour. Render it, do not persist it.

CreatedProduct.description: The stored product row. `id` is a bigint serialised as a string — always treat it as a string, never parse it into a JS number.

status.description: Always `draft` on creation; nothing else can be returned here.

MyProductListItem.description: A product in the owner's inventory, with enough auction state for the list to say what can be done with it next. Only the fields specific to this endpoint are documented; the rest of the product is returned as-is.

latestAuction.description: The most recent auction on this product, or null if it has never been listed. A re-listed item has several; this is the one to show.

hasLiveAuction.description: True while latestAuction is pending or happening.

canCreateAuction.description: Whether POST /api/v1/auctions would accept this product_id right now (published, has an image, no live auction). Use it to disable the action instead of letting the seller fill in a form that is refused.

WonAuctionBidInfo.description: Auction summary for the won order

price.description: Final winning price of the auction

NotificationType.description: Mirrors NotificationType in src/modules/notification/enum/notification-type.enum.ts. Generate client types from this list rather than hardcoding it — the two drifting apart is what made clients switch on categories that no writer ever produced.

NotificationCategory.description: Mirrors NotificationCategory. Payment notifications carry `order`, not `payment`.

NotificationPriority.description: Mirrors NotificationPriority. Nothing writes `urgent` yet — it exists because GET /notifications/stats already reports a count for it. Handle it, do not expect it.

NotificationActor.description: Who caused the notification. Non-null only for `new_bid` and `bid_outbid`; every other type is system-generated and leaves this null. Deliberately narrowed to three columns: the actor is a stranger to the recipient, so the User row behind it (email, phone, admin status notes) must never reach the client.

avatarFileId.description: Id in the files table, not a URL. Presign it via GET /api/v1/files/:id/url.

Notification.description: One notification. The socket event `notification` emits this exact shape, so a client can append a pushed item to the list it fetched without reshaping it.

title.example: Bạn đã bị trả giá cao hơn

actionUrl.description: Relative path, never an absolute URL. Null for `account_locked` and `account_unlocked`; `/orders` for `auction_won`, `/orders/{orderId}` for `payment_reminder`, `/product/{auctionId}` for the rest.

relatedData.description: Shape depends on `type`. Auction and bid types carry `auction`; `auction_won` and `auction_lost` carry `finalPrice` where the others carry `currentPrice`, plus `yourBid`. `new_bid` adds `bidAmount`, `bid_outbid` adds `newBidAmount`. `payment_reminder` carries orderId/productName/amount/deadline and no auction at all, so it has no image. `account_locked` carries orderCount/totalAmount, `account_unlocked` carries nothing, and `account_suspended`/`account_banned` carry the admin's reason plus suspendedUntil (null for a ban).

image.description: Presigned URL, signed per request on both the REST and the socket path. Null when the product has no image. Render it, do not persist it.

reason.description: The admin's stated reason for the suspension or ban.

CategoryWithImage.description: Image-bearing fields of a category. Reads only ever expose `imageUrl`, minted per response; the durable `imageFileId` handle is write-only.

imageUrl.description: Presigned URL, valid for 1 hour, or null when the category has no image. Render it, do not persist it; re-read the category to refresh.

avatarFileId.description: Id in the files table. Re-sign an expired avatarUrl via GET /api/v1/files/:id/url

avatarUrl.description: Presigned URL, valid for 1 hour. Render it, do not persist it.

rank.description: Sorted server-side, starting at 1. Clients must not re-sort.

totalBidders.description: Every distinct bidder — never capped, even when uniqueBidders is.

totalBids.description: Every bid row, manual and proxy. Never capped.

truncated.description: True when there are more bidders than uniqueBidders carries.

watcherCount.description: People currently viewing the auction, deduped per logged-in user. Counted in-process, so it is only accurate on a single API instance.

amount.description: Always a number, never a string.

get.description:
Returns the authenticated user's wallet with current balance and status.
Every registered user has exactly one wallet, created automatically at registration.

The `balance` field reflects the **available** balance: pending withdrawal holds
have already been subtracted. To see the full breakdown, use `GET /api/v1/wallet/summary`.

401.description: Unauthorized — missing or invalid Bearer token

404.description: Wallet not found (should not happen for registered users)

get.description: Alias for `GET /api/v1/wallet`. Identical behavior.

Returns the authenticated user's ledger entries in reverse chronological order.
Uses **cursor-based pagination** (never OFFSET) for consistent results under concurrent writes.

Each entry includes `balanceAfter` — the wallet balance snapshot right after that entry was posted.
This lets the FE render a running balance column without recalculating.

**Cursor format:** The `nextCursor` value is an opaque base64 string. Pass it back as-is in `?cursor=`.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Filter by ledger entry type. Omit to return all types.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Filter entries created on or after this timestamp (ISO 8601)

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Filter entries created on or before this timestamp (ISO 8601)

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response's `nextCursor`

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of entries to return per page

get.summary: Get financial summary grouped by entry type
get.description:
Aggregates the authenticated user's ledger into `SUM(amount)` and `COUNT` per ledger type.
Useful for displaying a dashboard breakdown:
- Total deposited (`topup_success`)
- Total spent (`payment` — values are negative)
- Total earned (`payment_release`)
- Total withdrawn (`withdraw_hold` — values are negative)
- etc.

Optional date filters narrow the aggregation window.
Only types with at least one entry in the range are included in `byType`.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Aggregate entries created on or after this timestamp

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Aggregate entries created on or before this timestamp

post.summary: Initiate a wallet top-up via bank transfer
post.description:
Creates a pending transaction and returns QR code + bank transfer instructions.

**User flow:**
1. Call this endpoint with the desired amount.
2. Display the returned `qrCodeUrl` as a scannable QR image, or show `bankInfo` for manual transfer.
3. User transfers money to the displayed bank account with the exact `paymentCode` as the transfer note.
4. Sepay detects the incoming transfer and fires a webhook to the backend.
5. The backend credits the wallet automatically. Poll `GET /api/v1/wallet` to see the updated balance,
   or listen to the `wallet:topup_success` WebSocket event (room `user_<id>`, payload `{ transactionId, walletId, amount }`).

**Important:**
- The transfer note MUST contain the `paymentCode` exactly. If the user types it wrong,
  the money lands in the admin bank account but the wallet is not credited automatically.
  Admin must then reconcile manually via the adjustment endpoint.
- The amount credited is always taken from the actual bank transfer amount (Sepay payload),
  never from what the user requested here.

**Rate limited** to prevent abuse.

amount.description:
Amount to top up in VND. Accepts a decimal string (e.g. `"500000.00"`) or number.
Must be strictly positive.

200.description: Top-up QR code and payment instructions generated

400.description:
Validation error. Possible messages:
- `Amount is required`
- `Top-up amount must be strictly positive`

429.description: Too many requests — rate limit exceeded

post.summary: Create a withdrawal request
post.description:
Requests a withdrawal of funds from the wallet to an external bank account.

**Key behaviors:**
- The requested amount is **debited immediately** (`withdraw_hold`) so it cannot be spent elsewhere.
- The user will receive **exactly 100%** of the requested amount. No fees are deducted at withdrawal —
  the 5% platform fee was already collected when escrow was released to the seller.
- Each user may have **at most one open request** (status `pending` or `processing`) at a time.
  Attempting to create a second request returns `WITHDRAWAL_ALREADY_PENDING`.
- The SLA deadline is **10 calendar days** from creation (`deadlineAt`). Admin is alerted hourly
  for overdue requests but they are NOT auto-cancelled.
- The platform wallet (system account) is blocked from creating withdrawal requests.

**Admin workflow after creation:**
1. Admin lists pending requests via `GET /api/v1/admin/wallet/withdrawals?status=pending`
2. Admin marks as processing: `PATCH .../process`
3. Admin transfers money via bank app, uploads receipt
4. Admin confirms: `POST .../complete` with `proof_file_id`
— or rejects: `POST .../reject` with `reject_reason`

**Rate limited** to prevent abuse.

amount.description: Amount to withdraw in VND. Must be strictly positive and ≤ available balance.

bankAccountName.description: Account holder name as registered with the bank

bankCode.description: Bank code (e.g. MB, VCB, TCB, BIDV, ACB)

400.description:
Validation or business logic error. Possible messages:
- `amount is required`
- `Withdrawal amount must be strictly positive`
- `bankAccountNo, bankAccountName, and bankCode are required`
- `WITHDRAWAL_ALREADY_PENDING` — user already has an open request
- `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE` — not enough available balance

403.description:
Forbidden. Possible causes:
- `WALLET_LOCKED` — wallet is frozen
- `Platform wallet may not create a withdrawal request`

429.description: Too many requests — rate limit exceeded

get.description:
Returns the authenticated user's withdrawal requests in reverse chronological order.
Includes requests in all statuses (pending, processing, completed, rejected, cancelled).

**Status meaning for the UI:**
- `pending` — money is already held (deducted from balance). User may cancel via `DELETE /withdrawals/{id}`.
- `processing` — admin is transferring; cancel is no longer allowed (hide the cancel button).
- `completed` — transferred; `proofUrl` holds the bank receipt image.
- `rejected` — full amount returned to the wallet; show `rejectReason`.
- `cancelled` — user cancelled; full amount returned to the wallet.

Show `deadlineAt` (10-day SLA) on open requests. Only one request can be open
(`pending`/`processing`) at a time, so disable "Rút tiền" while one exists.

Pagination: pass the returned `nextCursor` as `cursor`; `nextCursor = null` means last page.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response

delete.description:
Cancels a withdrawal request and **refunds 100%** of the held amount back to the wallet.

**Rules:**
- Only the owner of the request may cancel it.
- Only requests with status `pending` can be cancelled.
- Once status is `processing`, the admin may have already initiated a bank transfer,
  so cancellation is blocked. The user must contact admin directly.
- Replaying a cancel on an already-cancelled request is **idempotent** — returns the
  cancelled request without error and without moving money again.

200.description: Withdrawal cancelled, funds refunded to wallet

400.description:
Cannot cancel. Possible messages:
- `Cannot cancel withdrawal with status "processing"` (or completed/rejected)

403.description: Forbidden — not the owner of this request

get.description:
Returns withdrawal requests across all users, with optional filters.

**Typical admin workflows:**
- View pending requests: `?status=pending`
- View overdue requests (past 10-day SLA): `?overdue=true`
- Review processing requests: `?status=processing`

When `overdue=true`, results are sorted by `deadline_at ASC` (most overdue first).
Otherwise, sorted by `id DESC` (newest first).

**Review context for the approval screen (display only — never changes the amount to transfer):**
- `items[].sourceBreakdown` — where the requester's money came from:
  `selfTopup` = total bank top-ups, `salesRevenue` = total sales payouts already net of the 5% fee.
  Show it as e.g. "Nguồn: 1.000.000đ tự nạp | 500.000đ doanh thu bán hàng".
  The withdrawal is always paid out at 100% of `amount`; there is no fee at this step.
- `totalUserLiability` — `SUM(wallets.balance)` across **all** wallets (platform wallet included).
  The system cannot read the admin bank balance, so show this figure next to the approve button
  and ask the admin to confirm the real bank account holds at least this much before transferring.

All money fields are decimal **strings** (e.g. `"1500000.00"`) — do not parse to float for arithmetic.

Admins also receive in-app notifications (category `system`, priority `urgent`):
`withdrawal_sla_overdue` hourly while any request is past its 10-day deadline
(`relatedData.withdrawalIds`), and `wallet_reconciliation_failed` from the nightly
reconciliation when an invariant breaks (`relatedData.failed`).

parameters.name: overdue
parameters.description:
If `true`, returns only `pending`/`processing` requests where `deadline_at < now()`.
These requests have exceeded the 10-day SLA and need urgent attention.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response

patch.description:
Moves a withdrawal request from `pending` → `processing`.
This is a **status change only** — no money moves, no ledger entry is written.

Meaning: the admin has acknowledged the request and is preparing to make the bank transfer.
Once in `processing`, the user can no longer cancel the request (the admin may have already
initiated the bank transfer outside the system).

**Idempotent:** calling this on an already-processing request returns it unchanged.

400.description:
Invalid state transition. Possible messages:
- `Cannot move withdrawal from status "completed" to processing`
- `Cannot move withdrawal from status "rejected" to processing`
- `Cannot move withdrawal from status "cancelled" to processing`

post.summary: Confirm withdrawal completed with bank receipt (Admin only)
post.description:
Closes the withdrawal by recording that the bank transfer has been made.

**Requirements:**
- `proof_file_id` is **mandatory** — the file ID of the bank transfer receipt, uploaded via the file module
  (`POST /api/v1/files` (multipart, field `file`, purpose `withdrawal_proof`)). Without proof, the request is rejected with 400.
- The request must be in `pending` or `processing` status.

**What happens:**
- A `withdraw_success` ledger entry is posted with amount `0.00` (closing the book —
  the debit already happened at creation via `withdraw_hold`).
- Status changes to `completed`.
- A notification is sent to the user (`WITHDRAWAL_COMPLETED`).

**Idempotent:** calling this on an already-completed request returns it unchanged.

**Important:** The system does NOT verify the actual bank transfer. The admin must confirm
they have actually transferred the money before calling this endpoint.

proof_file_id.description: File ID of the uploaded bank transfer receipt

400.description:
Validation error. Possible messages:
- `proof_file_id is required`
- `Proof file not found`
- `Cannot complete withdrawal with status "rejected"` (or cancelled)

post.summary: Reject a withdrawal request and refund (Admin only)
post.description:
Rejects a withdrawal request and **refunds 100%** of the held amount back to the user's wallet.

**What happens:**
- A `withdraw_failed` ledger entry is posted with `+amount` (refunding the hold).
- Status changes to `rejected`.
- A notification is sent to the user (`WITHDRAWAL_REJECTED`).

**Idempotent:** calling this on an already-rejected request returns it unchanged.

reject_reason.description: Reason for rejection (shown to user in notification)

200.description: Withdrawal rejected, funds refunded to wallet

400.description:
Invalid state. Possible messages:
- `Cannot reject withdrawal with status "completed"` (or cancelled)

get.summary: Financial overview from daily summaries (Admin only)
get.description:
Returns aggregated financial data from the `wallet_daily_summary` table.
**This endpoint does NOT scan the full ledger** — it reads pre-computed summaries
generated nightly at 01:00 by the reconciliation cron job.

Response includes:
- **Totals** across the date range: top-ups, payments, withdrawals, platform fees, active wallets
- **Daily breakdowns** for charting

If no `from`/`to` is specified, returns the most recent `limit` days (default 30, max 365).

**Note:** Today's data may not be available yet (generated at 01:00 for the previous day).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of daily records to return

get.description:
Shows all orders currently holding funds in escrow (`fund_status = 'held'`).

**Key information:**
- `totalEscrow` — sum of `total_amount` across all held orders
- `platformWalletBalance` — current platform wallet balance
- `isEscrowCovered` — **Invariant 3 check**: is platform balance ≥ total escrow?
  If `false`, this is a **critical financial integrity issue**.
- `orders` — paginated list sorted by `delivered_at ASC NULLS LAST`, so the **oldest
  delivered-but-unreleased orders surface first** (these need the most urgent attention).

**Use cases:**
- Daily escrow audit: verify `isEscrowCovered = true`
- Find stuck orders: look for orders where `delivered_at` is old but still `held`
- Before processing large withdrawals: check that the admin's bank account can cover obligations

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Pagination cursor for the orders list

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of held orders to return per page

post.summary: Manual wallet balance adjustment (Admin only)
post.description:
Safety valve for reconciliation. Creates an `adjustment` ledger entry to credit or debit a wallet.

**Primary use cases:**
1. **Missed webhook:** Money appeared in the admin's bank account (user transferred correctly)
   but the Sepay webhook never arrived. Admin confirms on bank statement, then credits the user's
   wallet via adjustment.
2. **Correction:** Fix a ledger error by posting a compensating entry (the ledger is append-only,
   so corrections are always new entries, never edits to existing ones).
3. **Goodwill credit:** Compensate a user for a platform issue.

**Required fields:**
- `walletId` — which wallet to adjust
- `amount` — positive to credit, negative to debit. Cannot be zero.
- `reason` — free-text explanation (stored in ledger metadata, visible in audit trail)
- `bank_reference` — bank transaction ID or statement reference for audit traceability

**Constraints:**
- Cannot push a wallet balance below zero (enforced by the ledger engine).
- Each adjustment gets a unique UUID-based idempotency key, so replays are not possible.
- The acting admin's ID is recorded in `metadata.admin_id`.

walletId.description: ID of the wallet to adjust

amount.description:
Adjustment amount. Positive = credit the wallet, negative = debit.
Cannot be zero. Decimal string with 2 places preferred.

reason.description:
Mandatory explanation. Stored in ledger metadata for audit trail.
Should include context like "Bank transfer confirmed on statement but webhook failed"
or "Goodwill credit for delayed order #123".
reason.example: Bank transfer confirmed on statement but webhook failed

bank_reference.description:
Bank transaction ID or statement reference number. Required for audit traceability.
Check the admin's bank statement for this value.

400.description:
Validation error. Possible messages:
- `walletId is required`
- `amount is required`
- `Adjustment amount cannot be zero`
- `reason is required`
- `bank_reference (bank transaction ID) is required in metadata`
- `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE` — debit would push balance below zero

post.summary: Sepay bank transfer webhook
post.description:
**Internal endpoint — called by Sepay, not by the FE.**

Receives bank transfer notifications from Sepay when money arrives in the admin's bank account.
Protected by `verifySepayWebhook` middleware (API key/signature verification).

**This is the only way real money enters the system.** Past this middleware is effectively
a money printer — the webhook creates wallet balances from nothing (backed by the real bank deposit).

**Routing logic based on transfer note:**
- Note matches `BIDY{orderId}` (e.g. `BIDY001`) → **Order payment flow** (QR direct):
  Credits buyer wallet via `topup_success`, then immediately debits via `payment` + `payment_escrow_in`.
  Handles underpaid (credits wallet, order stays unpaid) and overpaid (credits full amount,
  debits only order total, surplus stays in wallet).
- Note matches `BIDYTOPUP{txId}` → **Top-up flow**: Credits wallet via `topup_success`.
- Note unrecognizable → Logged for admin manual reconciliation, nothing credited.

**Always returns 200**, even on duplicates — returning an error would cause Sepay to retry.

200.description: Webhook processed (or duplicate detected). Always 200 to stop Sepay retries.

401.description: Invalid Sepay API key or signature

get.summary: List auctions won by the authenticated user
get.description:
Every order where the caller is the buyer (one order per won auction), newest first.
Use it for the "Đấu giá đã thắng / Cần thanh toán" screen.

Each order carries computed helpers so the FE does not recalculate deadlines:
- `paymentDeadline`, `daysRemaining` — time left to pay.
- `isOverdue` — unpaid and past the deadline (the account may be locked by the deadline job).
- `isUrgent` — less than 24h left.
- `paymentStatus` — `pending` | `processing` | `paid` | `cancelled` | `refunded` | `expired` | `overdue`.
- `fundStatus` — `none` | `held` | `released` | `refunded` (trạng thái escrow).
- `bidId` — the auction summary (`id`, `name`, `price`, `description`, `image`), `null` if the auction is gone.

`data.summary` gives counters for tabs/badges: `total`, `pending` (not overdue), `paid`, `overdue`.
To pay an order use `POST /orders/{id}/pay` (wallet balance) or `GET /orders/{id}/payment-qr` (bank QR).

get.description:
Aggregated reminder state over the caller's **unpaid** (`pending`) orders — meant for a global
banner/badge, not a per-order view (use `GET /orders/{id}/status` for that).

Response fields:
- `pendingCount`, `urgentCount` (< 24h left), `overdueCount`, `hasOverduePayments`.
- `nearestDeadline` — earliest unpaid deadline, `null` if nothing is pending.
- `warningLevel` — `none` | `low` (something pending) | `medium` (something < 24h) | `high` (something overdue).
  Map directly to banner colour.
- `accountStatus` — currently always `active`; do not rely on it for lock state.

post.description:
**DEPRECATED — do not use for new UI.** Legacy checkout from before the wallet ledger.
It only moves the orders to `processing` and records `transactions` rows; **no money moves**
(no wallet debit, no escrow). Completing it via `POST /orders/payment/{paymentId}/confirm`
marks orders `paid` without any payment being received.

Use instead:
- `POST /orders/{id}/pay` — pay from wallet balance.
- `GET /orders/{id}/payment-qr` — pay by bank transfer (QR); the SePay webhook confirms it.

Body: `orderIds` (non-empty array of the caller's `pending` orders), `paymentMethod` (string).
Returns `transactionId` (the payment group id to pass to `/confirm`), `totalAmount`, `orders`.
Fails (400) if any order is not the caller's, or is not `pending` — the whole batch is rejected.

post.summary: Confirm a pending payment
post.description:
**DEPRECATED — do not use for new UI.** Legacy checkout from before the wallet ledger.
It only moves the orders to `processing` and records `transactions` rows; **no money moves**
(no wallet debit, no escrow). Completing it via `POST /orders/payment/{paymentId}/confirm`
marks orders `paid` without any payment being received.

Use instead:
- `POST /orders/{id}/pay` — pay from wallet balance.
- `GET /orders/{id}/payment-qr` — pay by bank transfer (QR); the SePay webhook confirms it.

`paymentId` is the `transactionId` returned by `POST /orders/payment`. Marks every order in that
group `paid`. 404 when no `processing` transaction with that id belongs to the caller.

get.summary: Generate VietQR code for order payment
get.description:
Generates a VietQR code for the buyer to pay for an order via direct bank transfer (QR scan).

**User flow:**
1. FE calls this endpoint to get the QR code and bank details.
2. User scans the QR with their banking app and transfers the exact `amount`.
3. The transfer note is auto-filled with `paymentCode` (format: `BIDY{orderId padded to 3}`).
4. When Sepay detects the transfer, the webhook fires and the order is marked as paid.
5. FE should poll `GET /api/v1/orders/{id}/status` or listen for the `order:paid` WebSocket event.

**Payment flow (pass-through):**
The incoming money first credits the buyer's wallet (`topup_success`), then immediately
debits it (`payment`) and enters escrow (`payment_escrow_in`) — all in one atomic transaction.
This means the wallet transaction history shows a clean money-in / money-out pair.

**Underpaid:** If the user transfers less than `total_amount`, the money is credited to
their wallet but the order is NOT marked as paid. User can then top up more and use
`POST /api/v1/orders/{id}/pay` to complete payment from wallet balance.

**Overpaid:** Full amount is credited to wallet, only `total_amount` is debited.
Surplus stays in the wallet as available balance.

A pending `transactions` row is created for tracking.

200.description: QR image URL and payment instructions

amount.description: Total amount to pay in VND (integer, no decimals)

paymentCode.description:
Transfer note that MUST be included in the bank transfer.
Format: `BIDY{orderId padded to at least 3 digits}`.
This is how the webhook identifies which order the payment is for.

qrCodeUrl.description: VietQR image URL — render as `` for the user to scan

bankInfo.description: Bank account details for manual transfer (if QR scan is not possible)

paymentDeadline.description: Deadline for payment. After this, the order may be auto-expired.

paymentStatus.description: Current payment status of the order

403.description: Forbidden — caller is not the buyer of this order

get.summary: Get payment and fulfillment status of a specific order
get.description:
Current state of one order, readable by its **buyer or seller** (403 otherwise).
Use it to poll after showing a payment QR (the socket event `order:paid` is the primary signal;
poll this every few seconds as a fallback) and to render the order detail.

Response fields:
- `paymentStatus` — `pending` | `processing` | `paid` | `cancelled` | `refunded` | `expired` | `overdue`; `isPaid` is the boolean shortcut.
- `shippingStatus` — fulfillment state.
- `totalAmount` — number (final price + shipping); `paymentDeadline`.
- `fundStatus` — escrow state: `none` (unpaid) | `held` (paid, money in escrow) |
  `released` (seller received payout) | `refunded` (buyer refunded).
- `deliveredAt` — when shipping became `delivered`, `null` before that.
  FE should warn when `deliveredAt` is old but `fundStatus` is still `held` (admin has not released).
- `fund_status` / `delivered_at` — snake_case duplicates of the two fields above, kept for compatibility.

post.summary: Pay for an order using wallet balance
post.description:
Pays for an order by debiting the buyer's wallet balance.
This is the **wallet payment** path — the alternative to QR direct payment.

**Double-entry ledger:**
- Buyer wallet: `payment` (-total_amount)
- Platform wallet: `payment_escrow_in` (+total_amount)

**Preconditions (all checked, failure returns 400/403/404):**
- Caller must be the buyer (`order.buyer_id = current_user`)
- `order.payment_status` must be `pending`
- Current time must be before `payment_deadline`
- Buyer wallet must have sufficient balance (≥ `total_amount`)

**After success:**
- `payment_status` → `paid`
- `fund_status` → `held` (money in escrow until admin releases)
- `payment_channel` → `wallet`
- WebSocket event `order:paid` emitted to buyer and order room

**Idempotent:** If the order was already paid (duplicate click), the ledger's
idempotency key (`order_payment:{orderId}`) prevents double-debiting.

fundStatus.description: Escrow status — `held` means money is in platform escrow

400.description:
Payment not possible. Possible error messages:
- `ORDER_NOT_PAYABLE` — order is not in `pending` payment status
- `ORDER_PAYMENT_DEADLINE_EXPIRED` — payment window has closed
- `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE` — wallet balance is less than `total_amount`

403.description: Forbidden — caller is not the buyer of this order (`FORBIDDEN`)

404.description:
Not found. Possible errors:
- `ORDER_NOT_FOUND`
- Buyer wallet not found

post.summary: Release escrow payment to seller (Admin only)
post.description:
Releases funds from escrow to the seller's wallet, deducting the 5% platform fee.
**This is the only way money leaves escrow.** There is no auto-release cron.

**Fee calculation:**
- `platform_fee = ROUND(final_price × 0.05, 2)` — calculated on `final_price` only, NOT including `shipping_fee`
- `seller_payout = final_price + shipping_fee − platform_fee` — seller receives shipping fee in full

**Double-entry ledger (3 legs):**
1. Platform wallet: `payment_escrow_out` (−total_amount) — money leaves escrow
2. Seller wallet: `payment_release` (+seller_payout) — seller receives net amount
3. Platform wallet: `platform_fee` (+platform_fee) — platform keeps commission

**Preconditions:**
- `fund_status` must be `held`. Releasing an already-released order returns 400.
- Seller must have a wallet.

**After success:**
- `fund_status` → `released`
- `platform_fee`, `seller_payout`, `fee_rate`, `released_at`, `released_by` are snapshotted on the order
- Seller receives a `PAYMENT_RELEASED` notification
- WebSocket event `payment:released` emitted to seller

**Idempotent:** If release was already done, the `fund_status = 'held'` check prevents double-release.

sellerPayout.description: Net amount credited to seller (final_price + shipping_fee − platformFee)

releasedBy.description: Admin user ID who performed the release

400.description:
Invalid state. Possible messages:
- `Order fund status must be 'held' to release` — order already released, refunded, or not yet paid

404.description:
Not found. Possible errors:
- `ORDER_NOT_FOUND`
- `SELLER_WALLET_NOT_FOUND` — seller doesn't have a wallet

post.summary: Refund escrow payment to buyer (Admin only)
post.description:
Refunds the full escrow amount back to the buyer's wallet.
Used when an order is cancelled or has issues **before** escrow was released to seller.

**Important: No refund is possible after release.**
Once `fund_status = 'released'`, the money is in the seller's wallet and cannot be clawed back.
This is a deliberate design decision — no post-release disputes are handled by the platform.

**Double-entry ledger (2 legs):**
1. Platform wallet: `payment_escrow_out` (−total_amount) — money leaves escrow
2. Buyer wallet: `payment_refund` (+total_amount) — full amount returned to buyer

**Preconditions:**
- `fund_status` must be `held`. Refunding an already-released/refunded order returns 400.

**After success:**
- `payment_status` → `refunded`
- `fund_status` → `refunded`
- WebSocket event `order:refunded` emitted to buyer and order room

**Note:** The `PaymentDeadlineService` also calls this internally when an order expires
while funds are in escrow, to prevent money from being stranded.

200.description: Order refunded, full amount returned to buyer wallet

400.description:
Invalid state. Possible messages:
- `Order fund status must be 'held' to refund` — order already released, refunded, or not yet paid

404.description:
Not found. Possible errors:
- `ORDER_NOT_FOUND`
- Buyer wallet not found

post.summary: Create an auction directly (Admin only)
post.description:
ADMIN ONLY. Sellers file an auction request instead (POST /api/v1/auction-requests) and an admin's approval creates the auction; a seller calling this gets 403. Admins keep the direct path so they can list something without queueing a request to themselves.
Two modes.
EXISTING PRODUCT — send `product_id` and only the pricing/schedule fields. Name, category, condition, description and images all come from the product, so nothing is re-entered and no duplicate product is created. The product must be `active`, own at least one image, and have no pending or running auction.
In this mode `name`, `category_id`, `description`, `condition` and `images` are all REJECTED with 400 rather than ignored — sending one means you expect it to apply, and quietly dropping it would leave the seller looking at a listing that never took their edit. Change them through PATCH /api/v1/products/:id and /api/v1/products/:productId/images.
INLINE PRODUCT — omit `product_id` and send the product fields plus `images`. The product is created alongside the auction, already published.
This endpoint is multipart/form-data because of the inline mode; scalar fields are ordinary form fields.

product_id.description: Auction a product from /api/v1/me/products. When present this is the only source of product data: `name`, `category_id`, `description`, `condition` and `images` are rejected with 400, not ignored. Check `canCreateAuction` on the product before offering this action.

category_id.description: Inline mode only. Rejected with 400 alongside product_id.

description.description: Inline mode only. Rejected with 400 alongside product_id.

condition.description: Inline mode only. Rejected with 400 alongside product_id.

images.description: Inline mode only, max 5 MB each. Rejected with 400 when sent together with product_id.

quantity.description: Units of the product sold in this auction. The lot goes to a single winner, so every price above is for the whole lot, not per unit. Valid in both modes — it describes the sale, not the product, so it is accepted alongside product_id.

400.description: Invalid input, or a product-owned field (name, category_id, description, condition, images) sent alongside product_id

data.description: Only the image-bearing fields are documented here; the rest of the auction payload is returned as-is.

image.description: Presigned URLs, valid for 1 hour. Render them, do not persist them.

quantity.description: Units sold in this auction, going to one winner. Prices on this payload are for the whole lot, not per unit.

imageFileIds.description: Ids in the files table, parallel to `image` and in the same order. Use GET /api/v1/files/:id/url to re-sign an entry of `image` once it expires, without refetching the auction.

put.summary: Update an auction owned by the authenticated user

schema.description: Every field optional; only what you send is changed.

starting_price.description: Also resets current_price, which is safe only while pending.

quantity.description: Units in the lot. Editable only while the auction is still pending — once bidding has opened, changing the lot size would be a bait-and-switch on everyone who already bid.

400.description: Auction is no longer pending, or quantity is not a whole number >= 1

404.description: Auction not found, or not owned by the caller

delete.summary: Delete an auction owned by the authenticated user

post.summary: Withdraw your own auction, while it still has no bids
post.description:
Bidders commit against the closing time a listing advertised, so a seller cannot cut a contested auction short — that would hand them the choice of when to stop the price. Once any bid exists the auction runs to its end, and this returns 409 `AUCTION_HAS_BIDS`.
With no bids there is nobody to disadvantage, so a seller who listed by mistake can withdraw. The auction moves to `cancelled` and leaves every public listing. Nothing is refunded because bidding holds no money — escrow only exists once an order is created.
Read `totalBids` from the auction payload to decide whether to offer the action; no extra call is needed. Admins use PATCH /api/v1/admin/auctions/{id}/cancel instead, which has no bid precondition.

404.description: Auction not found, or owned by someone else — the two are deliberately indistinguishable (error_code AUCTION_NOT_FOUND)

409.description: `AUCTION_HAS_BIDS` when anyone has bid, or `AUCTION_NOT_CANCELLABLE` when the auction already ended or was cancelled

post.summary: Place a bid on an auction

limitBid.description: Ceiling for proxy bidding, required when isAuto is true

post.summary: Enable proxy (auto) bidding on an auction
post.description: Send only the ceiling. The server places the opening bid at the current minimum and raises it automatically when outbid, stopping at the ceiling; the step comes from the auction's own bidIncrement. Clients must not compute bid amounts — doing so races whoever bids in between.

200.description: Auto-bid enabled and the opening bid placed

400.description: Ceiling below the current minimum, or auction not biddable

get.summary: Read your own proxy-bidding state for an auction
get.description: Returns only the caller's own ceiling — never another bidder's.

delete.summary: Disable proxy (auto) bidding on an auction for the authenticated user

post.summary: Buy an auction immediately at its buy-now price

400.description: Rejected with a stable `error_code`: BUY_NOW_NOT_AVAILABLE (no buy-now price), AUCTION_NOT_ACTIVE (already ended or not started), SELLER_CANNOT_BUY, or MISSING_SHIPPING_ADDRESS (set one via /api/v1/users/addresses)

409.description: Bidding has passed the buy-now price (error_code BUY_NOW_PRICE_EXCEEDED)

get.summary: Get the authenticated user's bid history, paginated
get.description:
`stats` covers the caller's ENTIRE history, not the page — a "won" count that changed as you paged would not be describing what it claims to. It sits next to `history` rather than inside `pagination` for the same reason.
`actionType` and `auctionStatus` are separate filters because they are not the same axis: won/lost/buy_now are values on the bid row, while "still running" is a property of the auction. A single dropdown in the UI maps "Đang diễn ra" to `auctionStatus=happening` and the rest to `actionType`.

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description: `position` is deliberately not sortable — it is the rank recorded when the row was written and is nullable.

parameters.name: dateFrom
parameters.description: ISO 8601 date-time or a bare `YYYY-MM-DD`. Filters on the BID's createdAt, not the auction's. Inclusive.

parameters.name: dateTo
parameters.description: Same formats, inclusive. A bare date covers the whole day, so `2026-09-20` includes bids placed at 23:59 that day.

stats.description: Computed over the whole history, not the page.

active.description: Distinct auctions still happening, not bid rows.

post.summary: Ask for a product to be put up for auction
post.description:
Sellers no longer create auctions directly — POST /api/v1/auctions is admin only now. This files a request an admin approves, and the auction is created by that approval.
The product must already be published with at least one image and must not already be on the block; those are the same rules POST /auctions enforced, checked here AND again at approval, because the product can change while the request waits in the queue.
JSON, camelCase — unlike the old multipart auction form, which only existed because it carried image uploads. Images belong to the product.

400.description: Invalid payload, or endDate not after startDate (error_code INVALID_DATE_RANGE)

403.description: The product belongs to someone else

422.description: PRODUCT_NOT_AUCTIONABLE (not published, or has no image)

get.description: A seller can only read their own; someone else's answers 404 rather than 403, because whether a request id exists is not a stranger's business. Admins can read any.

404.description: Not found, or not yours (error_code REQUEST_NOT_FOUND)

patch.summary: Change the terms of a request you filed
patch.description: Allowed while `pending` only — an approved request is the record of what was agreed, and a rejected one is a closed decision. The product cannot be swapped: withdraw and file a new request instead.

409.description: The request is no longer pending (error_code REQUEST_NOT_PENDING)

delete.description: Sets it to `cancelled` rather than deleting the row, so the queue keeps a record of what was asked for and withdrawn. Pending requests only.

409.description: The request is no longer pending (error_code REQUEST_NOT_PENDING)

get.description: Oldest first — a review queue is worked front to back, so the request that has waited longest comes first.

patch.summary: Adjust a request's terms before approving it (Admin only)
patch.description: Approve takes no body on purpose, so an admin who wants different terms edits them here first. That keeps exactly one path from stored terms to a live auction, and leaves the row saying what was actually approved.

409.description: The request is no longer pending (error_code REQUEST_NOT_PENDING)

post.summary: Approve a request and create its auction (Admin only)
post.description:
Takes NO body. The auction is created from the terms stored on the request, in the same transaction — an approved request without its auction would be a listing the seller believes is live and nobody can find.
The product rules are re-checked here, not trusted from filing time: between the two the product may have been unpublished, deleted, or auctioned through another route, and approving on a stale check is what would produce two live auctions for one item.
A request whose start date has already passed opens immediately rather than waiting for a moment that is gone. If its END date has passed, approval is refused with `REQUEST_SCHEDULE_EXPIRED` — edit the dates first.
The seller is notified with `auction_request_approved`, carrying the new auction id.

409.description: `REQUEST_NOT_PENDING`, `REQUEST_SCHEDULE_EXPIRED`, or `PRODUCT_HAS_LIVE_AUCTION` when the product was auctioned meanwhile

422.description: PRODUCT_NOT_AUCTIONABLE (unpublished or lost its images meanwhile)

post.summary: Reject a request (Admin only)
post.description: `reason` is required and is shown to the seller. A "no" with no reason leaves them guessing what to change, and they will refile the same thing. The seller is notified with `auction_request_rejected`.

409.description: The request is no longer pending (error_code REQUEST_NOT_PENDING)

tags.name: Wallet
tags.description:
User wallet API — view balance, top up via bank transfer, withdraw funds, and view transaction history.

All monetary values are returned as **decimal strings** with exactly 2 decimal places (e.g. `"500000.00"`).
Never parse them as floating point; use string-based or integer arithmetic.

Every response is wrapped in the standard envelope:
```json
{ "status": "success" | "fail" | "error", "message": "...", "data": { ... } }
```
On errors, `data` is absent and `error_code` may be present instead.

tags.name: Admin Wallet
tags.description:
Admin-only wallet management — withdrawal processing, escrow monitoring, financial overview, and manual reconciliation.

All endpoints require `isAdmin` middleware (Bearer token from an account with `role = 'admin'`).

**Monetary values** are decimal strings with 2 decimal places (e.g. `"500000.00"`).
**Response envelope:** `{ "status": "success"|"fail"|"error", "message": "...", "data": {...} }`

tags.name: Admin Support
tags.description:
Admin-side support chat API.

**REST is for loading the chat list and history only. Replies go over Socket.IO.** `GET /chats` for the list, `GET /chats/:chatId/messages` once when opening a chat, then stay on the socket. `POST /chats/:chatId/messages` still works and is kept for non-interactive callers (scripts, integrations), but an admin panel that POSTs every reply hits the rate limiter for no benefit — the socket path saves through the same service before broadcasting.

Admin emits: `admin_join_all` (once after connect, for the notification rooms) · `admin_join_chat` {chatId} · `admin_send_message` {chatId, message, clientMessageId, messageType} · `admin_typing` {chatId, isTyping} · `admin_status_update` {chatId, status}.

Server emits: `admin_notification` {type: support_chat_created, chat} · `new_support_message` · `support_message_ack` {clientMessageId, status: saved|failed, messageId, createdAt, code} · `support_chat_typing` · `support_chat_read_receipt` · `support_chat_status_update`.

`admin_send_message` and `admin_status_update` both persist before they broadcast, so the socket path is not a fire-and-forget shortcut around the database. Reconcile optimistic bubbles on `support_message_ack` by `clientMessageId`, and dedupe `new_support_message` by `messageId`.
